docs.text: Smelt runs have kind of disappeared on Lake Michigan. I used to have a blast smelt fishing back in the day. Oh and nothing gets more Yooper then Da Yoopers. #PureMichigan www.youtube.com/watch?v=TkGb...

I would like to know why people are not fishing Smelt, they are so good. Most smelt in northern #Ontario are an invasive species and they're making lake trout smaller New research is trying to determine how invasive smelt spread throughout the Great Lakes basin www.cbc.ca/news/canada/...
I wove that basket on the shore of Lake Superior 12 years ago. I miss basket weaving — busy hands mean quiet brain
#FoodieFriday In case you haven't heard, new research has put smelt safely back on the menu! Give these tasty little Great Lakes fish a try: buff.ly/gAS4ofY

I know in my area, "smelting" is very common. I'm not personally a fan of smelts, but I remember how fun it was to go net them with my dad and grandpa at ungodly hours lol. #LakeSuperior smelts have just started running in my area.

They are sold fresh. There is a smelt run on the Great Lakes on spring. I’ve never fixed them myself, but they are breaded with flour, cornmeal, salt, and pepper and deep-fried or pan-fried (heads and insides removed). Very crispy and yummy.

reminds me of how i feel telling "americans" about the tens of thousands years old trails which existed to barter smelt fish oil as far east as the great lakes from the pacific northwest. smelt is also known regionally as eulachon/oolikin/hooligin/ en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grease_...
Why don’t we get smelt anymore? Are they protected? Do they no longer spawn in the Great Lakes? I haven’t seen them on a menu in over a decade.
Smelt have plummeted in numbers on Lake Michigan so we are all missing them.
Smelt fishing is very popular on Lake Michigan in the spring. It's actually pretty good! And it's not cheap to buy now.

The Great Lakes smelt fisheries are much, much smaller than they were in the 1970s and 1980s because of restored lake trout populations (smelt are invasive to the Great Lakes, but lake trout eat them).
The smelt are running on the south shore of Lake Superior. Now you know.

Well - a "Smelt fry" was when there was a smelt run - we're talking lake Michigan. You can net dozens of them, close to shore. I remember the heads being cut off, but other than that, they were lightly breaded (flour and cornmeal) and fried in Crisco in a cast iron skillet.

What I'd give for a good smelt fry. But smelt populations in the Great Lakes region has really suffered, so they're really only available in a small timeframe. I haven't had smelt in over 20 years :C
